title: OLST protocol
author: Arun Narasimhan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.smwec7e
materials: Somato-dendritic cell morphology - data processing and structure

This document describes the materials and methods used to process data generated from Oblique Light Sheet Tomography (OLST) to quantify the somatodendritic morphology of molecularly defined cell types.
Each dataset is associated with the following METADATA:
Date of clearing (start and end date)
Data processing server (e.g. brain2, brain5 etc.)
Update the parameters in the matlab command line.
seriesInputDirectory – the path to the Series_10um
Cell morphology detection & Registration to CCF space
Semantic Segmentation – a Matlab based image-processing toolbox.

steps.title: Acquire Serial Section Datasets
steps.instruction: Image brains using Oblique Light-Sheet Tomography (OLST) using a cell type specific Cre mouse line (e.g., Emx-Cre, Chat-Cre).

substeps.instruction: Acquire serial sections at x-y resolution = 0.4 micron and z resolution = 2.5 microns.
Collect 54-56 sections (physical thickness 250 microns each) depending on the rostro-caudal axial length of the brain.
Capture images using an Andor Zyla 4.2 sCMOS camera and stream via 10tap cameralink cable to be stored in proprietary *.dat (Mono-12packed bit) format.

steps.title: Perform Initial Volume Reconstruction
steps.instruction: Use Matlab and the 'reconstructOPTVolume.m' script to process raw data into a coronal orientation.

substeps.instruction: Unpack proprietary .dat data and save as 16-bit TIFF format.
Calculate the average of all image tiles to determine the illumination field.
Stitch images along the y-axis first and then the z-axis using either predetermined overlap or linear X and Y stage position information.
Downsize the sequence to 16% of original size (resulting in 2.5x2.5um) for viewing/registration purposes.
Shear and stitch the stack to achieve coronal orientation using the Stitching plugin in Fiji (options: blend, maximum intensity, no blending, mean, or median).

steps.title: Configure Reconstruction Script Parameters
steps.instruction: Set the following variables in the Matlab reconstruction script:

substeps.instruction: Param_file_name: Path to the Metadata (ParameterFile.json) in the root folder.
OutputDirectory: Path to store reconstructed data.
outputImageBitDepth: Set to 0 for 16-bit or 1 for 8-bit TIFF.
doIlluminationCorrection: Set to 0 for no correction or 1 for correction.

steps.title: Generate Downsampled Image Stacks
steps.instruction: Organize the reconstruction root folder into subfolders: Stitched_2pt5um, MaxIntProj, Stitched_10um, and Keptstack_10um, then process using Fiji.

substeps.instruction: Create a Fiji macro to stitch the 2.5um individual stacks.
Create a maximum intensity projection (MIP) of individual z-stacks and save in 'MaxIntProj'.
Create downsized images (~10um) of individual z-sections and save in 'Stitched_10um'.
Hard crop the volumetric image overlap along z using the Fiji substack option and save in 'Keptstack_10um' (resulting resolution: 10x10x1.76um).

steps.title: Create Near-Isotropic Wholebrain Volume
steps.instruction: Process the kept stack to create a standardized wholebrain volume using Fiji and Matlab.

substeps.instruction: Load all z-sections from 'Keptstack_10um' into Fiji and save as an image sequence in 'Series_10um'.

Subsample the series along z using the Matlab code 'zprojectseries.m' with 'projectEveryNthSlice' set to 6 and 'projectionType' set to 'max' to obtain a near-isotropic resolution of 10x10x10.6um; save as a TIFF stack in 'Wholebrain'.
Further downsize this image using the Scale function in ImageJ to a resolution of 25x25x26.5um and save as a stack in 'Wholebrain'.

steps.title: Perform Quality Control and Registration
steps.instruction: Verify acquisition quality and register the brain volume to the Common Coordinate Framework (CCF) space.

substeps.instruction: Visualize the 10x10x10.6um and 25x25x26.5um stacks in Fiji to check overall quality.

Register the 25um voxel downsampled brain to CCF space using the elastix toolbox (ITK-based) in two steps: affine registration followed by b-spline registration, using Mattes mutual information as the similarity measure.
Verify registration by opening the result file in the 'elastixOutput' folder, warping the fixed image, and checking for congruous edges and corners.

steps.title: Extract Neuronal Morphologies
steps.instruction: Detect and segment cell morphologies to generate SWC files.

substeps.instruction: Use a Segnet framework (Matlab) requiring an NVIDIA CUDA-enabled GPU to detect cytoplasmic signals via CNNs.
Alternatively, use the NeuroGPS package for automatic reconstruction of large-scale neuronal populations with dense neurites.
Save the resulting somatodendritic morphology information as .swc files.
Qualitatively assess morphology by overlapping the .swc files with raw images using the Simple Neurite Tracer plugin in Fiji.
Transform .swc files to CCF space using the registration parameters to determine region-wise morphology.

steps.title: Archive and Compress Data
steps.instruction: Compress raw data using 7-zip File Manager to save storage space.

substeps.instruction: Use the LZMA2 compression method with 'Ultra' compression level on the raw folders containing OLST acquisition tiles.
Document the raw data size before compression (~11 TB) and after compression (~5.2 TB).
Optionally convert Data Level 0 reconstructed images to JP2 file format.
